method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Management of tetanus-prone wounds' (Last updated October 2025), retrieved 2026-09-23. claims.claim: ⚠️ **Treat every wound other than a clean minor one as tetanus-prone.**
claims.source_text: All wounds, other than clean minor ones, should be considered tetanus-prone
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of tetanus-prone wounds' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_tetanusprone_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Check the immunisation history and immunise if it is incomplete or uncertain.** TIG may be needed if the primary course is incomplete or the tetanus history is uncertain.
claims.source_text: Check immunisation history and immunise if incomplete or uncertain … Tetanus immunoglobulin (TIG) may be required if child has an incomplete primary immunisation course or an uncertain tetanus immunisation history
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of tetanus-prone wounds' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_tetanusprone_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: Tetanus causes jaw spasm, trouble swallowing, painful muscle spasms and stiffness, seizures, headache and difficulty swallowing or breathing; it may need sedation or prolonged ventilation in ICU, and can be fatal.
claims.source_text: Symptoms of tetanus can include spasms of the jaw muscles, trouble swallowing, painful muscle spasms and muscle stiffness, seizures, headache and difficulty swallowing/breathing. It can require sedation or prolonged ventilation in ICU. It can be fatal in a small number of cases
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of tetanus-prone wounds' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_tetanusprone_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Schedule:** tetanus doses at 2, 4, 6 and 18 months and 4 years, with a booster at 12–13 years. **A complete primary course is 3 or more doses.**
claims.source_text: The recommended schedule for tetanus immunisation is doses at 2, 4, 6, 18 months and 4 years of age, with a further booster at 12-13 years … A complete primary course of tetanus immunisation is ≥3 doses
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of tetanus-prone wounds' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_tetanusprone_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: In Australia, tetanus-toxoid vaccines come only as **combination vaccines**, with pertussis, diphtheria and other antigens.
claims.source_text: Tetanus-toxoid vaccines are only available in Australia as combination vaccines that include other antigens such as pertussis and diphtheria
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of tetanus-prone wounds' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_tetanusprone_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tetanus-prone wounds:** any wound other than a clean minor cut · compound fractures · bites · deep penetrating wounds · foreign bodies (especially wood splinters) · pyogenic infection · extensive tissue damage (contusions, burns) · obvious soil, dust or horse-manure contamination (especially if topical disinfection is delayed more than 4 hours) · **reimplantation of an avulsed tooth**.
claims.source_text: Tetanus-prone wounds: Any wound other than a clean, minor cut Compound fractures Bite wounds Deep penetrating wounds Wounds containing foreign bodies (especially wood splinters) Wounds complicated by pyogenic infections Wounds with extensive tissue damage (eg contusions or burns) Any wound obviously contaminated with soil, dust or horse manure (especially if topical disinfection is delayed more than 4 hours) Reimplantation of an avulsed tooth
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of tetanus-prone wounds' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_tetanusprone_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Take an immunisation history** and discuss catch-up. Records: myGov (parents, or children over 14), My Health Record, or the Australian Immunisation Register via HPOS or the AIR enquiries line (1800 653 809).
claims.source_text: Take an immunisation history, discussing the need for catch-up immunisations where appropriate … A child's immunisation history statement is available for parents (or children >14 years old) through myGov or for health professionals via the child's My Health Record. It can also be obtained from the Australian Immunisation Register (AIR) via Health Professional Online Services (HPOS) or the AIR enquiries line (1800 653 809)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of tetanus-prone wounds' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_tetanusprone_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Clean, disinfect and treat the wound surgically if appropriate.**
claims.source_text: Wounds must be cleaned, disinfected and treated surgically if appropriate
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of tetanus-prone wounds' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_tetanusprone_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **3 or more doses — clean minor wound:** vaccine only if due for the routine booster or more than 10 years since the last booster. **Other wounds:** vaccine if more than 5 years since the last booster. **No TIG** in either case.
claims.source_text: History of tetanus immunisation Clean minor wounds Other wounds Tetanus vaccine Tetanus immunoglobulin* Tetanus vaccine Tetanus immunoglobulin* ≥3 doses Only if due for routine booster or >10 years since last booster NO If >5 years since last booster NO
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of tetanus-prone wounds' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_tetanusprone_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Fewer than 3 doses, uncertain, or unimmunised:** vaccine **and complete the course** for any wound; **add TIG for every wound other than a clean minor one.**
claims.source_text: History of tetanus immunisation Clean minor wounds Other wounds Tetanus vaccine Tetanus immunoglobulin* Tetanus vaccine Tetanus immunoglobulin* … <3 doses or uncertain or unimmunised YES (and complete course) NO YES (and complete course) YES
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of tetanus-prone wounds' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_tetanusprone_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **TIG 250 IU IM, as soon as practicable after the injury; 500 IU if more than 24 hours have elapsed.**
claims.source_text: The recommended dose for TIG is 250 IU IM. Give as soon as practicable after the injury. If more than 24 hours have elapsed, 500 IU should be given
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of tetanus-prone wounds' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_tetanusprone_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: TIG is viscous: **give it slowly through a 23 gauge needle**, split large volumes across different sites, and **use the opposite limb** if giving the vaccine at the same time.
claims.source_text: Because of its viscosity, TIG should be given slowly using a 23 gauge needle. Administer large volumes in divided doses at different sites. If giving at the same time as the tetanus vaccine, give into opposite limb
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of tetanus-prone wounds' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_tetanusprone_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: TIG reactions are very uncommon: injection-site pain, redness and stiffness; rarely mild fever, chills, drowsiness or itchy rash. **Seek expert advice if there are known antibodies to IgA or a previous allergy to immunoglobulin products.**
claims.source_text: TIG reactions are very uncommon. Possible reactions include pain, redness and stiffness at injection site. Rarely mild fever, chills, drowsiness or itchy rash. Seek expert advice if known antibodies to IgA or previous history of allergy to immunoglobulin products
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of tetanus-prone wounds' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_tetanusprone_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Significant humoral immune deficiency or HIV: TIG for all tetanus-prone wounds**. Discuss with a senior doctor or the immunology team.
claims.source_text: NB Children with a significant humoral immune deficiency or HIV require TIG for all tetanus-prone wounds. Discuss with senior doctor or immunology team
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of tetanus-prone wounds' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_tetanusprone_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Complete the tetanus schedule with the same vaccine brand if available**; otherwise use another brand of the same antigen combination.
claims.source_text: If available, complete the vaccination schedule for tetanus with the same vaccine brand. If not available, use an alternative brand of the same antigen combination
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of tetanus-prone wounds' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_tetanusprone_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **dTpa** has less diphtheria toxoid and pertussis antigen than DTPa, and is **for use over 10 years of age**.
claims.source_text: dTpa: less diphtheria toxoid and pertussis antigens than DTPa. For use for >10 years of age
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of tetanus-prone wounds' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_tetanusprone_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ATAGI recommends Infanrix hexa and Vaxelis up to 10 years of age; some centres use them up to 18 years when multiple vaccines are needed (e.g. catch-up, after chemotherapy or HSCT).
claims.source_text: * ATAGI recommends the use of Infanrix hexa and Vaxelis in children up to the age of 10 years. However, some centres recommend them for children up to 18 years of age in instances where multiple vaccines are required (eg catch up, post chemotherapy/post HSCT)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of tetanus-prone wounds' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_tetanusprone_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Side effects:** common — mild fever, unsettled behaviour and drowsiness in infants and young children; injection-site pain, redness and swelling in older children. Very rare — anaphylaxis, urticaria, peripheral neuropathy.
claims.source_text: Common: Infants and young children: mild fever, unsettled behaviour, drowsiness Older children: pain, redness and swelling at injection site Very rare: anaphylaxis, urticaria, peripheral neuropathy
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of tetanus-prone wounds' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_tetanusprone_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when** the wound has been treated, tetanus prevention given, and follow-up for catch-up immunisations arranged.
claims.source_text: Consider discharge when Wound has been treated and tetanus prevention given Follow-up for catch-up immunisations has been arranged
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Management of tetanus-prone wounds' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Management_of_tetanusprone_wounds/, retrieved 2026-09-23
